reply.english: There are five people in my family.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي عَائِلَتِكِ يَا مُنَى؟
dialogue.english: How many people are in your family, Muna?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.arabic: فِي عَائِلَتِي سِتَّةُ أَفْرَاد: أَبِي وَأُمِّي وَثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَة وَأَنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: fee 3aa2ilatee sittatu afraad: abee wa ummee wa thalaathatu ikhwa wa anaa.
dialogue.english: There are six people in my family: my father, my mother, three brothers and me.

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: And are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: لَا، مَا زِلْتُ أَعْزَب. وَأَنْتِ، هَلْ أَنْتِ مُتَزَوِّجَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa, maa ziltu a3zab. wa anti, hal anti mutazawwija?
dialogue.english: No, I'm still single. And you, are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: Yes, my husband is an engineer.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Do you have children?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a son and a daughter.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللَّه! مَا اسْمُ اِبْنِكِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a allaah! maa ismu ibnik?
dialogue.english: Wonderful! What's your son's name?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: His name is Omar, and my daughter's name is Sara.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: I wish them all the best.

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: Thank you, Khalid.

pair.english: How many people are in your family? (to a man)

response.english: There are five people in my family.
Yes, my husband is a doctor.

pair.english: Do you have brothers and sisters? (to a man)

response.english: I have a brother and two sisters.
This is my mother.

lessons.culture: In Fusha a family member is named with a possessive ending, so the ending ـِي means 'my' and أُمِّي is 'my mother'. Asking whether someone is married changes for a man and a woman, and it is polite to ask only once you know the person a little.

exercises.prompt: A colleague asks you: 'هَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَزَوِّج؟' Say you are still single.
exercises.tip: مَا زِلْتُ means 'I am still'; add the state after it.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: 'كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي عَائِلَتِكَ؟' Say there are five.
exercises.tip: فَرْد is one person; أَفْرَاد is the plural.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لِي أَخٌ وَ_____.' (I have a brother and two sisters.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـَانِ marks exactly two.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَلْ أَنْتِ _____؟' (Are you married? to a woman)
exercises.tip: The ending ـَة makes the word feminine.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I have a son and a daughter.'
exercises.tip: لَدَيَّ means 'I have', like لِي.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Are you married?' (to a woman)
exercises.tip: هَلْ opens a yes-or-no question.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'my sister'?
exercises.tip: أُخْت is sister, أَخ is brother.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks a man whether he is married?
exercises.tip: أَنْتَ is for a man, أَنْتِ for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَنْتَ / مُتَزَوِّج / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: هَلْ always comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'فِي / عَائِلَتِي / أَفْرَاد / خَمْسَةُ'.
exercises.tip: Start with فِي عَائِلَتِي, 'in my family'.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.english: I'm very hungry.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa aydan. ureedu an aakul.
dialogue.english: Me too. I want to eat.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Welcome. What would you like?

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: أُحِبُّ الْفَلَافِل. وَمَاذَا تُحِبِّين يَا نُورَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: u7ibbu al-falaafil. wa maathaa tu7ibbeen yaa Noora?
dialogue.english: I like falafel. And what do you like, Nora?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.english: I want chicken with rice.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: And what will you drink?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا عَطْشَانَة. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَ الْمَاء.
dialogue.english: I'm thirsty. I want to drink water.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: And I want coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Right away. Here you are, enjoy your meal.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: Thank you. Join us.

pair.english: What do you like to eat?

response.english: I like falafel.
Yes, I'm very hungry.
The bill is fifty riyals.
Thank you, join us.

lessons.culture: In Fusha people say هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا to someone who is eating and صِحَّةً وَعَافِيَة after a drink, and the host often answers تَفَضَّلْ مَعَنَا, an invitation to join. Sharing food is a sign of hospitality across the Arab world.

exercises.prompt: A waiter asks: 'مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَأْكُل؟' Say you like falafel.
exercises.tip: أُحِبُّ means 'I like'; the food follows it.

exercises.prompt: Someone starts eating near you. Wish them a good meal.
exercises.tip: It is said to a person while they eat.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أُرِيدُ أَنْ _____ الْمَاء.' (I want to drink water.)
exercises.tip: After أَنْ the verb ends with a fatha sound.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَنَا _____ جِدًّا.' (I'm very hungry, a woman speaking.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـَة makes the word feminine.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The bill, please.'
exercises.tip: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ means 'please'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I want to eat.'
exercises.tip: أُرِيدُ أَنْ is 'I want to'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'thirsty' (said by a man)?
exercises.tip: عَطْشَان is thirsty; جَائِع is hungry.

exercises.prompt: What do you say to someone who has just finished drinking?
exercises.tip: هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا is for someone still eating.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَنْ / أُرِيدُ / آكُل'.
exercises.tip: Start with أُرِيدُ, 'I want'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'هُوَ / كَمْ / الْحِسَاب'.
exercises.tip: كَمْ, 'how much', opens the question.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: How old are you, Khalid?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: I am thirty. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا فِي الْخَامِسَةِ وَالْعِشْرِين. هَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَزَوِّج؟
dialogue.transliteration: anaa fee al-khaamisati wal-3ishreen. hal anta mutazawwij?
dialogue.english: I am twenty-five. Are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, anaa mutazawwij wa ladayya tiflaan.
dialogue.english: Yes, I am married and I have two children.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Masha Allah. Where does your family live?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: نَسْكُنُ فِي جُدَّة. وَأَخِي الْأَكْبَر فِي الرِّيَاض.
dialogue.transliteration: naskunu fee Judda. wa akhee al-akbar fee ar-riyaad.
dialogue.english: We live in Jeddah. And my older brother is in Riyadh.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: What does your brother do?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: هُوَ طَبِيب. هُوَ طَوِيل وَمَرِح جِدًّا.
dialogue.transliteration: huwa tabeeb. huwa taweel wa mari7 jiddan.
dialogue.english: He is a doctor. He is tall and very funny.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: And your sister?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: My younger sister is kind. She is a student.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.transliteration: wa hal jadduka wa jaddatuka ma3akum?
dialogue.english: And are your grandparents with you?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, jaddee wa jaddatee yaskunaani ma3anaa.
dialogue.english: Yes, my grandparents live with us.

response.english: I am thirty years old.
Yes, I have two children.
They live in Jeddah.
I am an engineer.

lessons.culture: Fusha has separate words for each relative: عَمّ is a father's brother and خَال a mother's brother, so اِبْنُ عَمِّي and اِبْنُ خَالِي are different cousins. It is polite to answer a mention of someone's children with مَاشَاءَ اللَّه.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟' Say you are thirty years old.
exercises.tip: عُمْرِي means 'my age'; the number follows.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ؟' Say you are an engineer.
exercises.tip: No verb 'to be' is needed: أَنَا مُهَنْدِس.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هِيَ _____ جِدًّا.' (She is very kind.)
exercises.tip: With هِيَ the describing word takes ة.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لَدَيَّ _____.' (I have two children.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـان makes it 'two'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'My cousin is funny.'
exercises.tip: Start with the person, then the describing word.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I am married.' (a man speaking)
exercises.tip: A woman would say مُتَزَوِّجَة.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'tall'?
exercises.tip: طَوِيل is tall; قَصِير is short.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'my younger sister'?
exercises.tip: الصُّغْرَى is younger, الْكُبْرَى is older.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'تَسْكُنُ / أَيْنَ / عَائِلَتُكَ'.
exercises.tip: The question word أَيْنَ comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'جِدًّا / طَوِيل / هُوَ'.
exercises.tip: جِدًّا, 'very', goes after the word it strengthens.

reply.english: We will eat rice and fish.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.arabic: الْفَطُورُ عَلَى السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَة يَا أَحْمَد.
dialogue.english: Breakfast is at eight, Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا يَا أُمِّي. مَاذَا سَنَأْكُلُ عَلَى الْغَدَاء؟
dialogue.english: All right, Mum. What are we eating for lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.arabic: سَنَأْكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ وَالسَّمَك. سَاعِدْنِي فِي الطَّبْخ.
dialogue.transliteration: sana2kulu al-aruzza was-samak. saa3idnee fee at-tabkh.
dialogue.english: We will eat rice and fish. Help me cook.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Gladly. Shall I set the table?

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Yes, set the table. The food is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Pass me the salt, please.

dialogue.speaker: Father
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا لَذِيذ جِدًّا. شُكْرًا يَا أُمَّ أَحْمَد.
dialogue.transliteration: haathaa ladheedh jiddan. shukran yaa umma A7mad.
dialogue.english: This is very delicious. Thank you, Umm Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: More?

dialogue.speaker: Father
dialogue.english: More, please.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: I am full, thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.arabic: اِرْفَعِ الْمَائِدَة يَا أَحْمَد، وَالْعَشَاءُ فِي التَّاسِعَة.
dialogue.transliteration: irfa3i al-maa2ida yaa A7mad, wal-3ashaa2u fee at-taasi3a.
dialogue.english: Clear the table, Ahmad, and dinner is at nine.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: As you wish, Mum.

pair.english: What are we eating for lunch?

response.english: We will eat rice and fish.
At last, I am hungry.
No, thank you, I am full.
No, I do not eat meat.

lessons.culture: A Fusha-speaking host often keeps offering more food, and the guest says أَنَا شَبْعَان, 'I am full', after one or two polite refusals. The family usually eats from shared dishes on one table, so asking someone to pass something uses نَاوِلْنِي.

exercises.prompt: Your mother asks: 'الْمَزِيدَ؟' Politely say you want more.
exercises.tip: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ ends in kasra when speaking to a woman.

exercises.prompt: A guest offers you meat. Say you do not eat meat.
exercises.tip: لَا before the verb means 'I do not'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'الطَّعَامُ _____.' (The food is ready.)
exercises.tip: جَاهِز describes الطَّعَام.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'نَاوِلْنِي _____.' (Pass me the salt.)
exercises.tip: نَاوِلْنِي is 'pass me' (to a man).

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'This is delicious.'
exercises.tip: لَذِيذ is the Fusha word for delicious.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Help me cook.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: فِي links the help to the task.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'full' (after eating, said by a man)?
exercises.tip: شَبْعَان is full; جَائِع is hungry.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'Dinner is at nine'?
exercises.tip: الْعَشَاء is dinner; الْفَطُور is breakfast.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْمَائِدَة / جَهِّزِ'.
exercises.tip: The command comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'جَاهِز / الطَّعَامُ'.
exercises.tip: Name the thing first, then say it is ready.

reply.english: I have lived here for five years.
Yes, my neighbourhood is quiet and beautiful.
I am from a small city.

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.english: Welcome to the neighbourhood!

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. اِسْمِي أَحْمَد. اِنْتَقَلْتُ إِلَى هُنَا مِنَ الْقَرْيَة.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. ismee A7mad. intaqaltu ilaa hunaa mina al-qarya.
dialogue.english: Thank you. My name is Ahmad. I moved here from the village.

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.english: Where do you live, Ahmad?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: أَسْكُنُ فِي شَقَّةٍ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِد.
dialogue.transliteration: askunu fee shaqqatin qareeban mina al-masjid.
dialogue.english: I live in a flat near the mosque.

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.english: Do you like the neighbourhood?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، هُوَ هَادِئ جِدًّا. وَأَنْتَ، مُنْذُ مَتَى تَسْكُنُ هُنَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, huwa haadi2 jiddan. wa anta, mundhu mataa taskunu hunaa?
dialogue.english: Yes, it is very quiet. And you, how long have you lived here?

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.english: I have lived here for ten years.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: مَرْحَبًا، أَنَا لَيْلَى أُخْتُ أَحْمَد. هَلِ السُّوقُ بَعِيدٌ عَنْ هُنَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: mar7aban, anaa Layla ukhtu A7mad. hali as-sooqu ba3eedun 3an hunaa?
dialogue.english: Hello, I am Layla, Ahmad's sister. Is the market far from here?

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.arabic: لَا، السُّوقُ قَرِيب. خَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ مَشْيًا.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, as-sooqu qareeb. khamsu daqaa2iqa mashyan.
dialogue.english: No, the market is near. Five minutes on foot.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: And where is your house?

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.english: My house is at the end of this street.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: So you are our neighbour! That is nice.

dialogue.speaker: Neighbour
dialogue.transliteration: wa antum jeeraanee al-judud. ahlan wa sahlan.
dialogue.english: And you are my new neighbours. You are most welcome.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Thank you, our neighbour.

response.arabic: أَسْكُنُ فِي بَيْتٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الْمَسْجِد.
response.transliteration: askunu fee baytin qareebin mina al-masjid.
response.english: I live in a house near the mosque.

pair.english: How long have you lived here?

response.english: For two years.
Yes, but it is far from the market.

response.arabic: أَنَا مِنَ الْقَرْيَة، وَانْتَقَلْتُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَة.
response.transliteration: anaa mina al-qarya, wantaqaltu ilaa al-madeena.
response.english: I am from the village, and I moved to the city.

response.arabic: عُنْوَانِي شَارِعُ الْمَسْجِد، قَرِيبٌ مِنَ السُّوق.
response.english: My address is Mosque Street, near the market.

lessons.culture: In Arab and Muslim culture neighbours matter a great deal, so a newcomer is welcomed with أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي الْحَيّ and is soon asked where he lives and where he comes from. These questions are friendly, not nosy.

exercises.prompt: A neighbour asks you (a man): 'أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟' Say you live in a flat.
exercises.tip: أَسْكُنُ means 'I live (reside)' and فِي means 'in'.

exercises.prompt: A neighbour asks: 'هَلْ تُحِبُّ حَيَّكَ؟' Say yes, it is quiet.
exercises.tip: هَادِئ means quiet or calm.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَسْكُنُ _____ شَقَّة.' (I live in a flat.)
exercises.tip: فِي is the word for 'in' with a place.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'نَسْكُنُ _____ مِنَ الْمَسْجِد.' (We live near the mosque.)
exercises.tip: قَرِيبًا مِنْ means 'near'; the opposite is بَعِيدًا عَنْ.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مُنْذُ _____ تَسْكُنُ هُنَا؟' (How long have you lived here?)
exercises.tip: مُنْذُ مَتَى is 'since when'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I live in a house.'
exercises.tip: Say the verb first: أَسْكُنُ.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'What is your address?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: The ending ـكَ means 'your' to a man.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I moved here from the village.'
exercises.tip: اِنْتَقَلْتُ is 'I moved'; إِلَى is 'to' and مِنْ is 'from'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'neighbourhood'?
exercises.tip: حَيّ is a neighbourhood; شَارِع is a street.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'far from'?
exercises.tip: بَعِيدٌ takes عَنْ; قَرِيبٌ takes مِنْ.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'هُنَا / تَسْكُنُ / مُنْذُ / مَتَى'.
exercises.tip: The question word comes after مُنْذُ.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'شَقَّة / فِي / أَسْكُنُ'.
exercises.tip: Verb, then فِي, then the place.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Layla, is your new house big?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ يَا أَحْمَد، بَيْتُنَا كَبِيرٌ وَجَمِيل.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am yaa A7mad, baytunaa kabeerun wa jameel.
dialogue.english: Yes, Ahmad, our house is big and beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: How many floors does it have?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: It has two floors. And we have a small garden.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: How many rooms are in the house?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: فِيهِ خَمْسُ غُرَفٍ وَمَطْبَخٌ وَاسِعٌ وَشُرْفَة.
dialogue.transliteration: feehi khamsu ghurafin wa matbakhun waasi3un wa shurfa.
dialogue.english: It has five rooms, a spacious kitchen and a balcony.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Layla, is your room bright?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ يَا أُمِّي، النَّافِذَةُ كَبِيرَة وَالْغُرْفَةُ مُضِيئَة.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am yaa ummee, an-naafidhatu kabeera wal-ghurfatu mudee2a.
dialogue.english: Yes, Mum, the window is big and the room is bright.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Ahmad, come. Look at the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: What a beautiful view!

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: وَالشَّارِعُ هَادِئ. السُّوقُ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْبَيْت.
dialogue.transliteration: wash-shaari3u haadi2. as-sooqu qareebun mina al-bayt.
dialogue.english: And the street is quiet. The market is near the house.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: A very beautiful house! Congratulations.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: May God bless you.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Please, Ahmad, the tea is ready.

pair.english: How many floors does your house have?

response.english: My house has two floors.
No, our house is small but it is beautiful.
Yes, it has a big window.
Yes, we have a beautiful garden.

pair.english: Is the market near your house?

response.english: No, it is a little far.

lessons.culture: A guest compliments a home with مَا أَجْمَلَ بَيْتَكُمْ, 'how beautiful your home is', and the host answers بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ. Flat roofs are common in Arab cities, and families often sit on them in the summer evenings.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you (a man): 'كَمْ طَابِقًا فِي بَيْتِكَ؟' Say there are two floors.
exercises.tip: طَابِقَان is 'two floors'; two is shown by a special ending, not by a number word.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: 'هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ حَدِيقَة؟' Say yes, a small garden.
exercises.tip: عِنْدَنَا means 'we have' (literally 'at us').

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'بَيْتِي _____.' (My house is big.)
exercises.tip: The describing word follows the thing described.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'السُّوقُ _____ مِنْ بَيْتِي.' (The market is near my house.)
exercises.tip: قَرِيبٌ takes مِنْ; بَعِيدٌ takes عَنْ.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'كَمْ _____ فِي الشَّقَّة؟' (How many rooms are in the flat?)
exercises.tip: After كَمْ the thing counted is singular.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The flat is bright.'
exercises.tip: مُضِيئَة ends in ـة because شَقَّة is feminine.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The street is quiet.'
exercises.tip: هَادِئ is quiet or calm.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'We sit on the roof.'
exercises.tip: نَجْلِسُ is 'we sit'; عَلَى is 'on'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'roof'?
exercises.tip: بَاب is a door; نَافِذَة is a window.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'The house is old'?
exercises.tip: قَدِيم is old; جَدِيد is new.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'كَبِير / بَيْتِي'.
exercises.tip: Name the house first, then describe it.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'غُرْفَةُ / وَاسِعَة / الْجُلُوسِ'.
exercises.tip: غُرْفَةُ الْجُلُوسِ is one name, 'living room'.

reply.english: The kitchen is next to the living room.
The bathroom is on the right.
The stairs are behind the door.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا خَالِد. هَذَا بَيْتُنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan yaa Khaalid. haathaa baytunaa.
dialogue.english: Welcome, Khalid. This is our house.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: The living room is beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Welcome, Khalid.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Thank you, Umm Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: I have the key.

response.english: The kitchen is next to the living room.
The bathroom is on the right.
Yes, it is ready.

pair.english: Where is your bedroom? (to a man)

response.english: My bedroom is on the upper floor.

pair.english: Let us go to the garden.

response.english: Good idea.

lessons.culture: Many Arab homes keep a separate guest room, غُرْفَةُ الضُّيُوف, and a host often shows a visitor into it or the living room first, before the rest of the house. A flat roof, سَطْح, is used for hanging washing and for sitting out on summer evenings.

exercises.prompt: A guest asks: 'أَيْنَ الْحَمَّام؟' Tell him it is on the right.
exercises.tip: عَلَى الْيَمِين means on the right; عَلَى الْيَسَار means on the left.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'أَيْنَ الدَّرَج؟' Say the stairs are behind the door.
exercises.tip: خَلْفَ means behind.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'الْمَطْبَخُ _____ غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوس.' (The kitchen is next to the living room.)
exercises.tip: بِجَانِبِ ends in a kasra because it follows the preposition بِ.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'غُرْفَةُ _____ جَاهِزَة.' (The guest room is ready.)
exercises.tip: الضُّيُوف is the plural of ضَيْف, a guest.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَيَّا نَصْعَدْ إِلَى _____.' (Let us go up to the roof.)
exercises.tip: سَطْح is the flat roof you can walk on.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The living room is downstairs.'
exercises.tip: الطَّابِق الْأَرْضِيّ is the ground floor; الطَّابِق الْعُلْوِيّ is the upper floor.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Where is the kitchen?'
exercises.tip: أَيْنَ opens the question and the thing asked about follows.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'This is my bedroom.'
exercises.tip: هَذِهِ is 'this' for a feminine thing, and غُرْفَة is feminine.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'roof'?
exercises.tip: سَطْح is the roof; دَرَج is the stairs.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'balcony'?
exercises.tip: شُرْفَة is the balcony; مَمَرّ is the corridor.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْمَطْبَخ / أَيْنَ'.
exercises.tip: The question word comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'النَّوْمِ / الشُّرْفَةُ / بِجَانِبِ / غُرْفَةِ'.
exercises.tip: Name the place first, then where it is.

reply.english: It is next to the television.
The key is on the table.
I will bring it for you. (to a man)

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Come in, Khalid, this is your room.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Is there a mirror in the room?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Switch on the fan, please.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Layla, the washing machine does not work.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Good night, Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: And you too.

response.english: The key is on the table.
It is next to the television.
I will bring it for you. (to a man)
Right away.

pair.english: Is there a mirror in the room?

response.english: Yes, next to the wardrobe.

lessons.culture: A Fusha-speaking host often asks a guest هَلْ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى شَيْء؟, 'Do you need anything?', and the guest is welcome to ask for a blanket or a fan. In many Arab homes the television sits in the living room, where the family gathers in the evening.

exercises.prompt: Your host asks: 'هَلْ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى شَيْء؟' Say you need a blanket.
exercises.tip: أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى means 'I need'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'أَيْنَ الْمِفْتَاح؟' Say it is on the table.
exercises.tip: عَلَى means on.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'شَغِّلِ _____.' (Switch on the fan.)
exercises.tip: شَغِّلْ is the command 'switch on' for a machine or a light.

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ سَرِيرٌ فِي الْغُرْفَة.' (There is a bed in the room.)
exercises.tip: هُنَاكَ means 'there is' and the thing follows it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'الْغَسَّالَةُ لَا _____.' (The washing machine does not work.)
exercises.tip: تَعْمَل is 'it works', and لَا before it makes it 'does not work'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Switch off the light.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: أَطْفِئْ is 'switch off'; شَغِّلْ is 'switch on'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Open the window.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: اِفْتَحْ is 'open' and أَغْلِقْ is 'close'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The sofa is comfortable.'
exercises.tip: مُرِيحَة is the feminine form because أَرِيكَة is feminine.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'mirror'?
exercises.tip: مِرْآة is the mirror and مِرْوَحَة is the fan.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'carpet'?

too_formal.feedback: also a real word for a rug, but this lesson practises سَجَّادَة

exercises.tip: سَجَّادَة is the carpet and وِسَادَة is the pillow.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الضَّوْء / شَغِّلِ'.
exercises.tip: The command comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'التَّحَكُّم / أَيْنَ / جِهَازُ'.
exercises.tip: جِهَازُ التَّحَكُّم is 'the remote control'.

challenge.title: A family meal
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which two people talk about their families over a meal, say what they like to eat and drink, and ask for the bill.
required_elements: how many people are in each family
a brother or sister and whether one is married
what each person likes to eat
a wish for a good meal
the bill asked for and its price

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي عَائِلَتِكَ يَا فَهْد؟
dialogue.english: How many people are in your family, Fahd?

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: فِي عَائِلَتِي أَرْبَعَةُ أَفْرَاد. لِي أُخْتٌ وَاحِدَة، وَهِيَ مُتَزَوِّجَة.
dialogue.transliteration: fee 3aa2ilatee arba3atu afraad. lee ukhtun waa7ida, wa hiya mutazawwija.
dialogue.english: There are four people in my family. I have one sister, and she is married.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا جَائِعَة. مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَأْكُل؟
dialogue.transliteration: anaa jaa2i3a. maathaa tu7ibbu an ta2kul?
dialogue.english: I'm hungry. What do you like to eat?

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: أُحِبُّ الْفَلَافِل، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَ شَاي.
dialogue.transliteration: u7ibbu al-falaafil, wa ureedu an ashraba shaay.
dialogue.english: I like falafel, and I want to drink tea.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: And I want coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.english: Enjoy your meal.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا، تَفَضَّلْ مَعَنَا. الْحِسَابَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran, tafaddal ma3anaa. al-7isaaba min fadlika.
dialogue.english: Thank you, join us. The bill, please.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: The bill is thirty riyals.
